title: Metallic Materials — Bend Test
technical_committee: MED 04 (Mechanical Testing of Metals Sectional Committee)
scope: This standard specifies the method for determining the ability of metallic materials to undergo plastic deformation in bending. It applies to test pieces taken from metallic products (sheets, strips, plates, bars, sections, wire) as specified in the relevant product standard.
description: IS 1599 establishes the technical principles, testing equipment, test piece geometry, and defect evaluation for bend tests on metallic materials. The bend test consists of subjecting a test piece of round, square, rectangular, or polygonal cross-section to plastic deformation by bending around a former/mandrel without reversing the direction of flexure, followed by optical examination for surface fissures or cracks.

key_requirements.requirement: The test shall be carried out at ambient temperature between 10°C and 35°C unless otherwise specified.

key_requirements.parameter: Edge Rounding of Rectangular Test Pieces
key_requirements.requirement: The edges of rectangular test pieces shall be rounded with a radius (r) not exceeding 0.1 times the thickness (0.1a) to prevent premature corner notch failure.
The diameter of the bending mandrel or former shall conform strictly to the product specification ratio (d = k * a).
key_requirements.acceptable_limit: As specified in product standard (e.g. 1a to 5a)

key_requirements.requirement: The test piece shall be bent to the angle specified in the relevant product standard (typically 90°, 120°, or 180°).

After bending to the prescribed angle, the outer convex surface and sides of the test piece shall be visually inspected; no cracks, fissures, or tears visible without magnifying aids shall be permitted.
key_requirements.acceptable_limit: Zero visible cracks on convex surface
key_requirements.permissible_limit: Cracks at corners < 0.1a ignored unless origin is material flaw

sections.title: Scope
sections.content: This standard specifies the method for determining the ability of metallic materials to undergo plastic deformation in bending. This standard applies to test pieces taken from metallic products, as specified in the relevant product standard.

sections.title: Normative References
sections.content: The following referenced documents are indispensable for the application of this document: ISO 7438 Metallic materials — Bend test, IS 1608 Metallic materials — Tensile testing, IS 1786 High strength deformed steel bars and wires for concrete reinforcement.

sections.title: Symbols and Designations
sections.content: Key symbols used in the bend test: a = thickness or diameter of test piece; b = width of test piece; L = total length of test piece; l = distance between supports (l = d + 3a ± 0.5a); d = diameter of the mandrel or former; r = radius of edges of test piece; alpha = angle of bend.

subsections.title: Mandrel Diameter Ratio
subsections.content: The ratio of mandrel diameter to test piece thickness (d/a) determines the maximum tensile strain induced on the outer fibers during the bend test.

sections.title: Principle of Test
sections.content: The bend test consists of subjecting a test piece of round, square, rectangular, or polygonal cross-section to plastic deformation by bending around a former of known radius without reversing the direction of flexure.

sections.title: Testing Equipment
sections.content: The test shall be carried out in testing machines or presses equipped with bending devices (two supports and a mandrel, V-block, or clamp). Supports shall have hardened radius between 1 mm and 10 times test piece thickness.

sections.title: Test Piece Preparation
sections.content: Round, square, rectangular, or polygonal cross-section test pieces shall be used. Edges of rectangular pieces shall be rounded with a radius not exceeding 0.1a to eliminate machining burrs.

sections.title: Procedure
sections.content: The test is conducted at ambient temperature between 10°C and 35°C. The test piece is placed symmetrically on supports and bent by smoothly applying force through the mandrel at a speed <= 30 mm/min.

sections.title: Interpretation of Results
sections.content: Absence of surface cracks visible without magnifying aids on the tension side (convex surface) after bending is considered as evidence of meeting the standard requirement.

applicable_products_or_industries: Structural Steel Rolling Mills and Fabrication Units
Boiler, Pressure Vessel, and Heavy Plate Fabricators
Sheet Metal Stamping and Cold Forming Facilities
